Water of the Word
WAW-tur uv thuh WURD
noun phrase
From the Greek loutron tou hudatos en rhēmati in Ephesians 5:26, the washing of water by the word; the Word as the Spirit's cleansing instrument.

📖 Biblical Definition

The water of the word is the Holy Scripture as the instrument by which Christ sanctifies and cleanses His church. Paul writes that Christ loved the church and gave Himself for it, that He might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, that He might present it to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle. The figure draws on the cleansing power of water, but the apostle names the means plainly: it is the word that washes. As the body is made clean by water, so the soul is purified by the truth of God applied by the Spirit. Our Lord prayed for His own, sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth; and He told His disciples, now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. Thus sanctification is no mystical process apart from Scripture, nor a mere outward conformity, but the progressive cleansing of the soul as the Word of God dwells richly within and the Spirit wields it against indwelling sin. The Word convicts, instructs, reproves, and renews; it washes away the defilement of error and corruption; it conforms the believer to the image of Christ. This cleansing is ongoing, the daily work of grace in the Christian life, for the church is being sanctified now and shall be presented glorious at the last. Here is the great means God has appointed: His own Word, read, preached, and believed, washing the bride He purchased with His blood.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The Scripture as Christ's appointed means of sanctifying and cleansing His church.

expand to see more

WATER OF THE WORD, noun phrase. From the Greek loutron tou hudatos en rhēmati, the washing of water by the word.

The Holy Scripture viewed as the cleansing instrument by which Christ sanctifies His people.

A figure drawn from water's cleansing power, applied to the purifying truth of God.

Paul writes in Ephesians 5:26 that Christ sanctifies the church, "cleansing it with the washing of water by the word."

The ordinary means of progressive sanctification, the Word wielded by the Spirit against indwelling sin.

📖 Key Scripture

Eph 5:26 — "That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word,"

Joh 17:17 — "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth."

Joh 15:3 — "Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you."

Psa 119:9 — "Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Sanctification is sought in inner feeling, technique, or experience while the cleansing Word is neglected.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Yet the practical neglect of the Word as the means of sanctification is everywhere. Many seek holiness through inner feeling, programs, or private spiritual experiences while the appointed laver—the Scripture itself—lies unopened and unread. The result is a religion of sentiment that produces no cleansing, for it bypasses the very instrument Christ has ordained to wash His church.

To recover the truth we must return to the water of the word as the primary means of grace. Christ sanctifies His bride by the washing of His Word, applied by the Spirit, and there is no cleansing of the soul that does not flow through Scripture read, preached, sung, and obeyed. Therefore the believer who would grow in holiness must dwell in the Word, letting it convict, reprove, instruct, and renew, until he is conformed to the image of the Christ who gave Himself for the church.

Usage

"The believer feeds daily on the water of the word that he may be cleansed and sanctified."

"Pastors preach the Word knowing it is Christ's appointed means of washing the church."

"Growth in holiness is sought through Scripture, not through feeling apart from it."
